# Spring Boot REST API with Kotlin & Gradle — Comprehensive Learning Guide

## Course Overview

This intermediate-level course teaches you how to build production-ready REST APIs using **Spring Boot**, **Kotlin**, and **Gradle** — three modern technologies that have become standard in enterprise backend development. You'll move beyond basic CRUD operations to understand dependency injection, testing strategies, configuration management, and API design patterns that matter in real-world systems.

**Who it's for:**
- Developers with 1–2 years of experience in Java or another JVM language
- Backend engineers transitioning to Kotlin
- Those preparing for senior backend or full-stack roles at tech companies

**Why it matters for interview prep:**
- Spring Boot is ubiquitous in enterprise tech stacks (Google, Netflix, Amazon, Spotify)
- Kotlin syntax and null-safety features are increasingly tested in coding rounds
- Building a complete API from scratch is a common system design and implementation interview topic
- Gradle and dependency management round out practical DevOps knowledge

---

## Core Topics Covered

- **Kotlin Fundamentals & Spring Integration** — syntax, data classes, extension functions, null-safety, and how Kotlin differs from Java in a Spring context
- **Spring Boot Core Concepts** — auto-configuration, starters, application properties, profiles, and embedded servers
- **Building REST APIs** — HTTP verbs, routing, request/response handling, status codes, and RESTful principles
- **Dependency Injection & Bean Lifecycle** — @Component, @Service, @Repository, constructor injection, scopes, and circular dependency resolution
- **Data Access with Spring Data JPA** — entity mapping, repositories, custom queries, transactions, and N+1 query prevention
- **Validation & Error Handling** — @Valid, custom validators, exception handling, error response formatting
- **Testing Strategies** — unit tests, integration tests, mocking with Mockito, TestContainers, and test slices
- **Gradle Build Tool** — dependency management, multi-module projects, custom tasks, build optimization

---

## Learning Path Workflow

### **Phase 1: Kotlin & Spring Boot Foundations (Tasks 1–12)**
1. Set up a Kotlin + Spring Boot project with Gradle
2. Understand Kotlin data classes and null-safety
3. Create your first `@RestController` endpoint
4. Explore Spring Boot auto-configuration
5. Use application.yml for configuration management
6. Implement constructor-based dependency injection
7. Work with Kotlin extension functions in Spring context
8. Understand Spring Bean lifecycle and scopes
9. Configure multiple profiles (dev, test, prod)
10. Use Gradle to manage dependencies
11. Debug Spring Boot startup and context loading
12. Understand Spring's component scanning and stereotype annotations

### **Phase 2: REST API Design & HTTP Fundamentals (Tasks 13–25)**
13. Implement GET endpoints with path variables and query parameters
14. Create POST endpoints with @RequestBody
15. Handle PUT and PATCH for resource updates
16. Implement DELETE endpoints
17. Return proper HTTP status codes
18. Use @ResponseEntity for fine-grained response control
19. Implement pagination and sorting
20. Add content negotiation (JSON, XML)
21. Implement API versioning strategies
22. Use @RequestHeader and @CookieValue
23. Implement request validation with @Valid
24. Create custom error response objects
25. Use Spring's built-in exception handlers

### **Phase 3: Data Persistence & JPA (Tasks 26–40)**
26. Define JPA entities with Kotlin data classes
27. Configure Spring Data JPA repositories
28. Perform basic CRUD operations
29. Use derived query methods (findByName, findByEmailAndAge)
30. Implement custom queries with @Query
31. Use JPQL and native SQL queries
32. Implement pagination in repositories
33. Handle database transactions with @Transactional
34. Configure lazy vs. eager loading
35. Implement one-to-many relationships
36. Implement many-to-many relationships
37. Use @Projection for DTO projection
38. Prevent N+1 query problems with fetch joins
39. Use database migrations with Flyway
40. Handle timestamp and audit fields with @CreationTimestamp, @UpdateTimestamp

### **Phase 4: Advanced Spring & API Patterns (Tasks 41–55)**
41. Implement global exception handling with @ControllerAdvice
42. Create custom validators
43. Use @Aspect for cross-cutting concerns (logging, timing)
44. Implement service layer with business logic
45. Create DTOs and use MapStruct for mapping
46. Implement the Builder pattern in Kotlin
47. Use Kotlin sealed classes for type-safe results
48. Implement request/response interceptors
49. Add request logging and request IDs
50. Implement rate limiting
51. Use Spring Security basics (authentication/authorization)
52. Implement JWT token handling
53. Use Spring's caching annotations (@Cacheable, @CacheEvict)
54. Implement async endpoints with @Async
55. Handle large file uploads and streaming responses

### **Phase 5: Testing & Quality Assurance (Tasks 56–65)**
56. Write unit tests with JUnit 5 and Mockito
57. Mock Spring beans with @MockBean
58. Test REST controllers with MockMvc
59. Write integration tests with @SpringBootTest
60. Use TestContainers for database testing
61. Test data layer with @DataJpaTest
62. Test service layer with @WebMvcTest
63. Implement test fixtures and builders
64. Achieve code coverage with JaCoCo
65. Test async and scheduled operations

### **Phase 6: Build, Deploy & Production Readiness (Tasks 66–74)**
66. Configure Gradle multi-module projects
67. Use Gradle plugins for Spring Boot builds
68. Manage dependency versions with dependency management
69. Create executable JAR files
70. Configure production logging with Logback
71. Implement health checks and metrics with Actuator
72. Monitor API performance with custom metrics
73. Dockerize a Spring Boot application
74. Implement graceful shutdown and startup probes

---

## Key Skills You'll Build

### **Backend Architecture**
- Design RESTful APIs that follow HATEOAS principles
- Structure projects with clear separation of concerns (controller → service → repository)
- Use domain-driven design patterns

### **Kotlin-Specific Patterns**
- Leverage null-safety to eliminate `NullPointerException` bugs
- Use data classes, sealed classes, and extension functions idiomatically
- Write concise, expressive code that reduces boilerplate

### **Spring Framework Mastery**
- Understand dependency injection at a deep level (how Spring resolves beans)
- Configure Spring Boot for different environments
- Use Spring Data abstractions effectively
- Implement cross-cutting concerns with AOP

### **Database Design & Optimization**
- Model complex relationships (one-to-many, many-to-many, hierarchical)
- Write efficient queries and prevent N+1 problems
- Understand transaction isolation levels and deadlock prevention
- Manage database schema evolution

### **Testing & Code Quality**
- Write testable code by design (dependency injection, separation of concerns)
- Achieve high code coverage with unit and integration tests
- Use mocking and stubbing effectively
- Understand test pyramid strategy

### **Build Tooling & DevOps**
- Use Gradle as a build and dependency management tool
- Manage complex dependency graphs
- Create reproducible builds
- Containerize applications for deployment

---

## Sample Problem Types

### **Problem Type 1: Building a Multi-Entity REST API with Relationships**

**Description:**  
Create a blog platform API with `User`, `Post`, and `Comment` entities. Users have many posts; posts have many comments. Implement endpoints to:
- Create a user and retrieve all their posts (paginated)
- Create a post for a user
- Add comments to a post
- Delete a comment (with permission checks)

**Key Skills Tested:**
- Entity modeling and relationships (one-to-many, cascade behavior)
- Repository custom queries
- Pagination and sorting
- Request validation
- Authorization checks

**Code Sketch:**

```kotlin
// Entity definitions
@Entity
data class User(
    @Id @GeneratedValue val id: Long = 0,
    val name: String,
    @OneToMany(mappedBy = "author", cascade = [CascadeType.ALL])
    val posts: List<Post> = emptyList()
)

@Entity
data class Post(
    @Id @GeneratedValue val id: Long = 0,
    val title: String,
    val content: String,
    @ManyToOne val author: User,
    @OneToMany(mappedBy = "post", cascade = [CascadeType.ALL])
    val comments: List<Comment> = empty
